title: Ofgem publishes the energy price cap for 1 July to 30 September 2027 — a Wednesday ceiling, and no Wednesday ceiling has ever been beaten (0 of 4); the control-quarter premise that created this entry is refuted
source: EST: ofgem.gov.uk/news/changes-energy-price-cap-between-1-october-and-31-december-2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-11 (HTTP 200) by this event's own initial research rather than inherited from the proposer — Ofgem's 26 August 2026 cap release, under 'Energy price cap level dates', reads verbatim 'The levels for the next periods will be announced by: ... 26 May 2027 - period 1 July 2027 to 30 September 2027', followed by 'We may publish before these dates if we need to because of external reasons'. EST: rather than a confirmed prefix on four counts, only the first of which is about the date itself. (1) The stem is 'by', and the announcement-date record this lane assembled is 7 cycles deep with 2 early publications, so the day is a ceiling, not a slot. (2) This is the furthest-out of three dates on a disclosure convention that is ONE RELEASE OLD: Ofgem named exactly ONE forward date in every release this lane could source through 27 May 2026 ('The levels for the period 1 July to 30 September 2026 will be published by 27 May 2026', Apr-Jun 2026 release; 'by 26 August 2026', Jul-Sep 2026 release, both fetched 2026-09-11, both singular 'before this date'), and first published a THREE-period slate on 26 August 2026. A date knowable three quarters out only because of a one-off format change carries convention risk the nearer two do not. (3) This lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. (4) market-events-data.ts defines no confirmed prefix for a UK sector regulator. Proposed 2026-09-09 by the ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2026-11-25 lane; canonical file written 2026-09-11 by this lane's never-assessed initial research, its proposal read in full first
notes: ITS STATED REASON FOR EXISTING IS REFUTED, TWICE, AND IT IS CARRIED ANYWAY ON DIFFERENT GROUNDS. The proposing lane filed this as 'the CONTROL for the VAT reversion' — the clean quarter that would let the April 2027 step be split into tax versus wholesale. The ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2027-02-23 lane refuted that the same day from Ofgem's press releases (Ofgem itemises components in pounds as practice and named the VAT counterfactual unprompted). This lane refutes it a second, independent way from the cost-allowance annex: Ofgem's 1 July 2026 letter publishes VAT as its OWN LINE in the Direct Debit cost breakdown, with a percentage, alongside wholesale / networks / operating / policy / EBIT / headroom / levelisation, every quarter. The April 2027 decomposition is a table lookup, not an inference, and it needs no control quarter. What the entry is carried for instead: (a) it is the calendar's Ofgem HORIZON — the furthest date Ofgem publishes, so the next pulse's job is to pick up the Oct-Dec 2027 date when the February 2027 release names it; (b) it is the WEDNESDAY CONTROL on this lane's date finding — all 7 sourced cycles are explained by ceiling day-of-week except one, Wednesday ceilings are 0-for-4 beaten and Tuesday ceilings 2-of-3 beaten, and the forward slate's only Tuesday is the SIBLING'S 2027-02-23, which is where that hypothesis actually gets falsified; (c) the Apr->Jul 2027 step is the first one after the reversion that is VAT-clean on both sides. Tiered LOW and unchanged from the proposal: symbols [], no UK listing, utility, gilt or sterling instrument anywhere in this calendar's eight-name US universe, and no house playbook keyed to energy or sterling. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
